reception.text: A search of California papers from mid-May to mid-June 1905 found no notice of the Panama proclamation.

related.note: The 1902 Cuban vessels proclamation used the same section 4228 authority, with differently worded operative clauses.

uncertain: When and through whom Panama supplied the proof recited in the proclamation, and whether the Treasury or the Canal Commission pressed for it, is not known.

reception.text: The Bern copyright bureau's journal reprinted the proclamation with Norway's matching decree, noted that its text was identical to the proclamations for other countries, and treated the exchange as routine.
A search of California papers from late June through August 1905 found no notice of the Norway proclamation.

political_impact.text: The proclamation was one half of a matched pair: a Norwegian royal decree of May 25, 1905, extended Norway's copyright law to future American works from July 1, 1905, the date Roosevelt signed.

legacy.text: Norway was later folded into collective copyright proclamations, including the multi-country proclamation of April 9, 1910.

later_actions.text: A multi-country copyright proclamation included Norway.

related.note: Copyright had been extended to Cuba by the same section-13 route in 1903.

uncertain: Whether the proclamation drew notice in the Norwegian-language American press or the book-trade press has not been checked.
